title: Debugging steps card
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Programming sequences and online safety
source: Seeded from computing/y3 lesson 5 (Debugging steps card (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 5: Debugging: find and fix errors. To understand how to find and fix a bug by testing a script one step at a time

questions.q: Fix the script on the slide so it draws a square.
questions.a: Move 'turn right 90 degrees' inside the repeat, under 'move 100 steps'.
questions.model: Teacher drags the turn block inside the loop, predicts 'a square', then runs it to prove it.

questions.q: Bug: 'repeat 4 (move 100, turn 45)'. What does it draw and how do you fix it?
questions.a: Half of an octagon; change turn 45 to turn 90.

questions.q: Bug: nothing is drawn but the sprite moves. Why?
Core: Open the class project 'Buggy shapes' and fix the three scripts (square, triangle, dashes).
questions.a: Square: turn inside the loop; triangle: turn 120 not 90; dashes: add pen up.
questions.model: Teacher fixes the square first, saying each debugging step aloud.

questions.q: Extend: Write in the portal response box what each bug was and how you found it. Start: 'The script should... but it...'
questions.a: For example: The script should draw a triangle but it drew part of a square, so I changed turn 90 to turn 120.

questions.q: Stretch: Make a script with one bug for a partner to find in the next lesson.
questions.a: A script with one clear bug and the fix written down.

questions.q: Debugging means... A) deleting the program B) finding and fixing mistakes C) adding more blocks
What should you always do after fixing a bug?
